reproduction_target: DAWN-SCAPE method application: from third-party bulk-RNA-seq expression matrix (Gandal et al.) plus DE and AP significance metrics (Gandal et al.; Fu et al.; Wan et al.; Liu et al.), run p-to-z conversion and Efron locfdr recalibration, gene filtering, Partial Neighborhood Selection (PNS, l1-regularized neighborhood selection) network construction, four-state joint-HMRF hidden-state inference over an initialization-threshold grid, stable Two-Step Leiden + consensus clustering, cluster labeling by if-else composition rules, and downstream cell-type marker (Seurat FindMarkers on Velmeshev et al. snRNA-seq) and GO/SynGO enrichment. No wet-lab work is performed in this paper; all reported experiments are secondary analyses of published data.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-analysis extracted from Methods (main) plus Supplementary Sections S1.2-S1.3 (Description of Datasets, Details of Pipeline), which carry essentially all of the operational detail. Upstream Gandal-et-al. preprocessing (CPM/RSEM gene filtering, limma-trend + CQN normalization, WGCNA NetworkConcepts outlier removal, lmerTest technical-covariate regression) is described but is inherited third-party preprocessing, folded into C1 rather than verdicted separately. The WGCNA-module comparison in Results is folded into C8 (WGCNA is used there to subdivide large AD clusters). NO code-availability statement, NO data-availability statement, and NO repository URL of any kind (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Zenodo/figshare/OSF/Code Ocean/Software Heritage) appears anywhere in the JATS full text; a case-insensitive scan of the full text for those hosts returns zero matches. No software version number is stated for any tool or R package anywhere in the paper.

steps.label: Input assembly: bulk cortex RNA-seq expression matrix (54 neurotypical controls, from Gandal et al. [1], 24 836 genes x 725 samples after upstream limma-trend/CQN normalization, WGCNA outlier removal, lmerTest covariate regression) + DE q/p-values (ASD: Gandal et al. [1]; AD: Fu et al. [13]) + AP p-values (ASD: Wan et al. [33]; AD: Liu et al. [30] combined with 53 fixed common/rare-variant genes [31,32])

q-value to p-value transform, p-to-z conversion, and replacement of infinite z-scores by equally spaced values between floor/ceiling of the two largest finite z-scores plus N(0,0.001) noise (custom procedure, random draw, no seed stated)

Calibration assessment and recalibration of DE z-scores using Efron's locfdr method [19] (two-component null/signal mixture; MLE null N(0.537,1.477) for ASD, N(0.892,1.58) for AD); AP z-scores left unadjusted

Gene filtering prior to network construction: intersect expression / DE / AP gene sets, drop genes with <50% non-zero cells, retain the 8 000 highest-mean-expression genes; forced inclusion of 52 of 53 AD 'fixed' genes with AP p set to 0.0 and DE p set to 0.5 when absent

Network construction by Partial Neighborhood Selection (PNS) [5]: key set = union of genes in smallest 10% of DE or AP p-values; correlation filter tau = 0.5 for core set S and neighbor set N; l1-regularized (LASSO) Meinshausen-Buhlmann neighborhood selection with regularization parameter lambda chosen by average degree / power-law R2 / degree-one proportion / average shortest path / stable-edge proportion / CV-MSE / visual inspection (lambda values reported in Supplementary Table S1)

Four-state joint-HMRF inference (Algorithms 1-2, ICM optimization) run over an initialization-threshold grid for 100 iterations - ASD {0.01,...,0.15} x {0.01,...,0.15} step 0.01; AD {0.05,...,0.50} x {0.05,...,0.50} step 0.05 - then manual selection of five runs 'in a relatively stable region' with sufficient active genes, majority vote across the five state labels with ties resolved to the lower state

Stable Two-Step Leiden clustering (Algorithm 3; Leiden [12] then embedding-similarity hierarchical re-merge to k clusters), hyperparameter grid search over (resolution r, k) with s = 100 random seeds per pair, scored by scaled modularity + silhouette (on the bulk expression matrix) + mean pairwise ARI, followed by consensus-matrix hierarchical clustering at the selected (r', k')
Manual subdivision of large clusters (>= 250 genes): ASD clusters cut into two or three components 'based on the structure of the dendrogram'; AD large clusters subdivided using WGCNA [7]
Cluster labeling as Etiological / Emergent / Other via if-else rules on within-cluster and by-state composition proportions (thresholds given in the supplementary if-else rule table)

Cell-type-specific marker gene derivation with Seurat FindMarkers [21,22] on the Velmeshev et al. [20] snRNA-seq dataset, then per-cluster marker enrichment testing (major cell types: excitatory/inhibitory neurons, microglia, astrocytes, OPC, oligodendrocytes, pericytes, vascular)

Functional enrichment with clusterProfiler enrichGO [24,25] with Benjamini-Hochberg [26] multiple-testing correction, plus SynGO [27] synapse-specific enrichment; run both per-cluster and pooled by cluster type (Supplementary Tables S8-S10)

headline.static_readiness: 0/11 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: All 11 computational steps cap at NI even under the most generous inference-inclusive reading. The blocking condition is absolute rather than marginal: the paper provides no code repository and no code-availability statement of any kind, so the novel components (PNS invocation, four-state joint-HMRF, Two-Step Leiden, consensus clustering, if-else cluster labeling) exist only as pseudocode in the supplement; and no software version is stated for any tool or R package anywhere in the text, so the version axis is 0 for every step. Two steps additionally depend on undocumented human judgement (C6 'select five runs in a relatively stable region'; C8 manual dendrogram-based subdivision of large ASD clusters). Parameter reporting is by contrast unusually good (explicit grids, tau = 0.5, 8 000-gene cut, s = 100 seeds, lambda in Table S1), but parameters cannot lift a step whose code and version axes are 0.
headline.coverage: 11 computational steps assessed from Methods prose plus Supplementary Sections S1.2-S1.3; 0 wet-lab steps (W = 0, no experiments performed in this paper). No data-availability and no code-availability section is present.

gaps.missing: No code repository, scripts, notebooks, package, commands, or configuration files are provided anywhere in the paper, and there is no code-availability statement. The method is novel (joint four-state HMRF, Two-Step Leiden, stability/consensus wrapper) and exists only as prose plus pseudocode Algorithms 1-3 in the supplement, so no executable artifact exists for a stage-2 read.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the DAWN-SCAPE implementation as an R/Python package or analysis repository (GitHub + archived Zenodo DOI) containing the PNS driver, joint-HMRF inference, Two-Step Leiden, consensus clustering, labeling rules, and the per-application driver scripts, and cite it in a Code Availability section.

gaps.where: Software environment for every named tool (locfdr, LASSO/neighborhood-selection implementation, Leiden, WGCNA, Seurat, clusterProfiler, SynGO, limma/lmerTest in inherited preprocessing)
gaps.missing: No version number, no R/Python version, no sessionInfo, no conda environment, no renv lockfile, no container. The version axis is 0 for all 11 steps; capture_claim is 'none'.
gaps.how_to_close: Record exact package versions (sessionInfo / renv.lock or conda-lock) and ideally ship a container digest alongside the code repository.

gaps.missing: No accession, URL, or repository identifier is given for any input: the Gandal et al. bulk expression matrix and WGCNA modules, the ASD DE q-values, the AD DE p-values (Fu et al.), the ASD AP p-values (Wan et al.), the AD AP p-values (Liu et al.) plus the 53 fixed genes, and the Velmeshev et al. snRNA-seq data are all referenced by citation only. There is no data-availability statement.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a Data Availability section listing the concrete accessions/URLs (e.g. the Synapse/psychENCODE identifiers for the expression matrix and the exact supplementary tables of each source paper) and deposit the harmonized DE/AP z-score input files actually consumed by the pipeline.

gaps.missing: Stochastic steps with no random seed reported: the infinite-z-score replacement adds N(0,0.001) noise and randomly assigns replacement values; Two-Step Leiden is run over s = 100 unspecified random seeds; consensus clustering aggregates those runs. Exact numerical reproduction of the published cluster assignments is therefore not possible from the prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Report or ship the seeds (and the RNG/backend) used for the reported runs, or provide the consensus matrices as intermediate artifacts.

gaps.missing: Human-judgement and unstated-parameter points: C6 selects 'five runs in a relatively stable region' with no stated selection rule; C7 does not state the resolution set or k set searched; C8 subdivides large ASD clusters 'based on the structure of the dendrogram' (manual) and uses WGCNA for AD with no stated soft power / merge parameters; C10 gives no Seurat FindMarkers parameters (test, logFC/pct thresholds) and no enrichment test definition for the marker-overlap testing.
gaps.how_to_close: State the run-selection criterion as an explicit rule, list the searched (r, k) grids, give the WGCNA and Seurat parameter settings, and either automate or fully document the manual cluster subdivision.

gaps.missing: GO/SynGO annotation database versions and enrichGO settings (ontology, universe/background gene set, p/q cutoffs, minGSSize) are unstated; enrichment results drift with annotation releases.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the OrgDb/GO.db and SynGO release versions and report the background gene universe and significance cutoffs used.
